Before I draft the plan, one decision changes the design a lot.

Your wording (“TypeScript … from the perspective of the extension” + avoid rebuild/reinstall so the kernel stays up) reads as a **live extension-host TypeScript REPL**: snippets transpile/eval inside the already-loaded extension, with helpers like `vscode`, active notebook, and `kernel.executeCode(...)`, so you can prototype extension logic without an Extension Host restart.

Please confirm which of these you want:

1. **Extension-host TypeScript REPL** (recommended from your description) — run TS in the extension process; call into the Jupyter kernel via existing APIs (`getKernel` / `executeCode`). Kernel stays alive because the extension never reloads.
2. **Kernel console only** — UI to send **Python** (or kernel language) to the active kernel; not really TypeScript execution in the extension.
3. **Both** — TS REPL in the extension host *and* a convenient “send this string to the kernel” helper in the same panel.

Also: should this be a **developer-only** feature (default off, gated like other `jupyter-cell-tags.features.*` flags), or something end users would normally open?

Reply with `1` / `2` / `3` and whether it’s **dev-only** or **user-facing**, and I’ll lock the plan.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I have enough to create a solid plan.

The feature will be developer-only and off by default.

The architecture splits into a `src/liveConsole/` module with startup, panel, evaluator, and API files. It will use a `liveConsole` feature flag and the command `jupyter-cell-tags.liveConsole.open`. Code from the webview will be transpiled with `typescript.transpileModule` and evaluated via `AsyncFunction`.

The evaluator will wrap code in an async IIFE with injected bindings. It will capture console output and return values, serialize results, and post them back to the webview. The exposed API will include VS Code, notebook and cell helpers, kernel access, and a kernel execution helper.

Direct `require` of extension modules is too brittle due to path issues. A relative `load` helper is preferable. The main benefit is iterating new features without rebuilding.

The console will execute code typed directly into it, avoiding rebuilds for prototyping snippets. Loading from disk files is deferred to a later phase. Multi-line TypeScript will be supported. Top-level await is under consideration.

Top-level await will be supported via AsyncFunction. Serialization will use JSON for primitives and Node's util.inspect for complex objects. A security warning will be included in the feature description.

The UI will be a WebviewPanel beside the active editor. It will show a status line, a code textarea, Run and Clear buttons, an output area, and support Ctrl/Cmd+Enter to run. It will also include data-testid attributes.

No new npm dependencies are needed. The built-in TypeScript package's transpileModule will be used.

Tests will cover unit evaluation, console capture, and syntax errors. Host tests will verify command registration when the feature is enabled.

I need to resolve a test conflict. The registration test requires every package.json command to be registered. Feature-gated commands unregister when the toggle is off. Existing tests likely enable all features in workspace settings. I will follow that pattern.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I have a clear picture. Let me implement:

First I will update featureFlags.ts and package.json.

Next I will create the liveConsole module files, wire them into extension.ts, and add tests. I also noticed a packaging issue: TypeScript is currently a devDependency, but the runtime evaluator needs it to call transpileModule. I will likely move it to dependencies or use a bundled approach.

I am defining the LiveConsoleApi interface. It will expose methods to access the active notebook and cells, locate notebook editors, retrieve the kernel, execute code, and describe console status.

I am designing the evaluator API. It will reuse mime decoding from executeCode but return structured results instead of logging. The EvalResult type captures execution status, value text, error text, logs, and duration. The evaluateTypeScript function will wrap user code in a strict async IIFE and inject the vscode module and LiveConsoleApi bindings.

I am considering using `AsyncFunction` to dynamically create the evaluator function with injected bindings. For expressions that do not explicitly return a value, I will try to detect the last statement and rewrite it to return that value, following a common REPL pattern.

I decided against auto-wrapping single expressions with `return`. Users will need to explicitly return values, similar to a standard REPL.

I am reconsidering the explicit return requirement. The plan specifies that last expressions should be shown, so I will implement a simple last-expression return helper instead. I rejected TypeScript parsing as overkill and am exploring a lightweight wrapper pattern for the evaluator.

I settled on the final evaluator design. The transpiled code will run as the body of an AsyncFunction with injected `vscode`, `api`, and `console` parameters. Single-expression inputs will be auto-wrapped with `return` so the last value is captured. I rejected the `with` statement as unsafe.

The `coerceReturn` helper is finalized. It wraps single-line expressions that are not statements with `return`. The status object will include notebook metadata and kernel availability. I am now implementing all files.
</details></think>

Implementing feature-flag wiring and the core `liveConsole` module next.

_**Agent (default)**_

Live extension-host TypeScript console is in place.

**Enable:** `jupyter-cell-tags.features.liveConsole` (default off) → command **Jupyter Cell Tags: Open Live TypeScript Console**.

**How it works:** Snippets transpile with `typescript.transpileModule` and run via `AsyncFunction` in the extension host with `vscode`, `api`, and a bridged `console` — no Extension Host reload, so the Jupyter kernel stays up.

```146:155:src/liveConsole/evaluator.ts
	try {
		const js = transpileTypeScript(source);
		const AsyncFunction = getAsyncFunctionConstructor();
		const runner = new AsyncFunction(
			'vscode',
			'api',
			'console',
			`"use strict";\n${js}\n//# sourceURL=jupyter-cell-tags-live-console.js`
		);
		const value = await runner(bindings.vscode, bindings.api, bridgedConsole);
```

**`api` helpers:** `getActiveNotebook` / `getActiveCell(s)`, `getKernel()`, `executeOnKernel(code)`, `describeStatus()`.

**Layout:** New module under `src/liveConsole/` (evaluator, API, webview panel, startup), wired through `optionalFeatures` in `extension.ts`. `typescript` is a runtime dependency for transpile.

**Tests:** Unit suite passes (`npm run test:unit`, 35 tests). Host smoke in `liveConsole.vscode.test.ts`; feature enabled in the test workspace settings.
